name: By The Wine
seoTitle: By The Wine, Chiado: Portuguese Wine by the Glass
tagline: A Chiado wine bar pouring Sogrape's Portuguese wines and ports by the glass, with tapas-style plates

description.short: By The Wine is a wine bar and restaurant on Rua das Flores in Chiado, opened in 2015. Since 2021 its list has been built around Sogrape, Portugal's largest wine producer: Douro, Dão, Alentejo, Vinho Verde and Port, much of it by the glass, with Portuguese and Spanish small plates.
description.full:
By The Wine suits a port day only if you check the day of the week. The Portuguese version of its website gives Lisbon hours of 19:00 to midnight from Monday to Wednesday and 13:00 to midnight from Thursday to Sunday; the English page still says Tuesday to Sunday from 13:00. In August it opens only in the evening, from 18:00. On a typical day call that sails in the early evening, aim for a Thursday to Sunday lunch, and call ahead on +351 213 420 319 to confirm.

From the terminal it is about 1.8 km and 27 minutes on foot: west along the river to Praça do Comércio, then up through the Baixa into Chiado, with a short climb at the end. Rua das Flores runs downhill from Largo do Camões, so you can also take the metro to Baixa-Chiado and walk about five minutes. A taxi takes 8 to 10 minutes.

The point of coming is to taste Portuguese wine without committing to a bottle. Glasses start at around €4 and run to about €15 for top Douro and Port; ask for a Dão white or a Douro red, and finish with a Sandeman or Ferreira port. The food is shared plates, mostly €6.50 to €27, such as octopus carpaccio, garlic prawns, codfish salad and a loin-steak prego sandwich. Bread, olive oil and butter arrive as a €5 couvert; send it back if you do not want it.

Lunch on Thursday to Sunday is the calmest time. Evenings, especially Friday and Saturday, are busier, and the website takes reservations. If you want to take a bottle back on board, the wine list has separate, lower 'drink out' prices for bottles to go, but check your cruise line's policy on bringing alcohol aboard.

Skip it on a Monday to Wednesday day call: it will not open until after most ships have sailed.
description.history: By The Wine opened on Rua das Flores in 2015, originally as a showcase for the wines of José Maria da Fonseca, the Setúbal producer. In March 2021 it switched to Sogrape, Portugal's largest wine group, founded in 1942 and known worldwide for Mateus Rosé. Since then the list has centred on Sogrape's Portuguese estates, including Casa Ferreirinha in the Douro, Quinta dos Carvalhais in the Dão, Herdade do Peso in the Alentejo, Quinta da Romeira near Lisbon and the Sandeman and Ferreira port houses, plus its properties in Spain, Chile, Argentina and New Zealand. In November 2024 a second By The Wine opened in Porto.
description.significance: For a visitor with a few hours, it offers a structured tasting of Portugal's main wine regions in one sitting: Vinho Verde, Dão, Douro, Alentejo, Bucelas and Port, most available by the glass at modest prices. Because the list belongs largely to one producer it is not a neutral survey, but it covers the main grape styles and both table wine and Port.

directions.general: Located on Rua das Flores in the historic Chiado shopping district, near Praça Luís de Camões
directions.fromCruisePort: About 1.8 km and 27 minutes on foot: west along the river to Praça do Comércio, then up through the Baixa towards Chiado (the final streets climb). Taxi about 8-10 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Baixa-Chiado station (Blue/Green lines) 5-minute walk. Tram 28 stops nearby. Bus routes 758, 760 serve the area.
directions.parking: Limited street parking. Public parking at Praça Luís de Camões or Armazéns do Chiado parking garage (5-minute walk).

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily; afternoons only from Thursday to Sunday (check by phone: the official site's Portuguese and English pages differ)

seasonal.notes: Per the Portuguese page of bythewine.pt. The English page lists Monday only as evening-only, so Tuesday and Wednesday lunch may also be possible: call to confirm.

admissionPrices.notes: No entry fee. Lisbon menu and wine list (2026): wine by the glass about €3.90–€15; shared plates about €6.50–€27; couvert €5 (charged only if you eat it). Bottles to take away are sold at lower 'drink out' prices.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: About 1–1.5 hours for a few glasses and shared plates
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Thursday to Sunday lunch, from 13:00. Evenings, especially Friday and Saturday, are busiest; reserve for dinner.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Hours differ between the official site's Portuguese and English pages, so phone +351 213 420 319 before planning around a lunchtime visit. Reservations are available through the website. Most wines are poured by the glass, so ask staff to suggest a short sequence across regions.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2–2.5 hours: 20–27 minutes each way plus 1–1.5 hours at the table
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Mostly flat walk along the river to Praça do Comércio, then a moderate climb into Chiado; the metro to Baixa-Chiado shortens it. Ground-floor venue; phone ahead about steps at the entrance and space between tables.
combinableWith: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
tips: Go Thursday to Sunday from 13:00; on Monday to Wednesday it opens at 19:00, after most day-call sail-aways.
Phone +351 213 420 319 to confirm hours: the official site's Portuguese and English pages give different weekday times.
In August it opens only from 18:00 every day, which rules out lunch.
Order by the glass (from about €3.90) to compare regions: for example a Vinho Verde, a Dão white, a Douro red and a port.
The €5 couvert (bread, olive oil, butter, olives) is charged only if you eat it; send it back if you do not want it.
From Baixa-Chiado metro, walk to Largo do Camões and down Rua das Flores: about five minutes.
Bottles to take away are priced lower than to drink in, but check your cruise line's rules on bringing wine aboard.
Allow 27 minutes to walk back to the terminal, mostly downhill and then flat along the river.

highlights: Around 80 wines, centred on Sogrape's Portuguese estates
Most wines available by the glass
Sandeman and Ferreira ports, from ruby and tawny to LBV
Douro, Dão, Alentejo, Vinho Verde and Bucelas whites and reds
Shared plates such as octopus carpaccio, garlic prawns and codfish salad
Lower 'drink out' prices for bottles to take away

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Ground floor venue, may have one or two steps at entrance. Narrow space between tables. Best to call ahead regarding specific accessibility needs.
